ROUND 4, FINDING 1 — CORRECTED BY THIS REVIEW. THE MODEL DECLARES A FULL TEACHING COLOUR KEY AND NOT ONE PIXEL OF IT REACHED THE STUDENT. Every beat in this scene rendered in a single flat lilac. MEASURED in the real player (walk-scene-in-player, my own run, same bytes the build run proved): across beats 1, 2, 4 and 13 every lit pixel fell in two adjacent 30-degree hue bins with median saturation 0.083. The model's OWN render harness, on the SAME model file, gives median saturation 0.468 spread over six hue families — so the model was never the problem. ROOT CAUSE, read out of viz3d.js and then confirmed in the player: line 604 builds a material as s.color, THEN the model's palette, THEN the neutral '#c9c3d8', and its own comment says exactly that. But restyle() — line 2427, which runs on EVERY view — is m.material.color.copy(srgbColor(isSel ? glow : s.color, '#c9c3d8')) and has no knowledge of the model palette. With no s.color it repainted all 34 structures '#c9c3d8' the moment any beat was applied, discarding the correct palette line 604 had just installed. THIS SCENE IS THE ONLY ONE IN THE CORPUS WHOSE STRUCTURES CARRY NO color (checked against body-cavity-coelom and heart-external, which both do), which is why it is the only one that ever reached that fallback, and why the player looks fine on every other scene. WHAT A STUDENT LOST: beat 1 drew foregut, midgut and hindgut as ONE UNIFORM TUBE, so 'one tube, three divisions' showed no three; beat 2 drew the aorta and all three arteries in the same colour as the gut they supply, so 'three arteries cut the tube into three' showed no cut; beat 4, whose narration calls the two beads 'the two sentences to memorise verbatim', drew both beads the same colour as each other and as everything else. FIXED by giving each structure the colour the model already declares for the part its ref resolves to — LAYERS copied verbatim, nothing invented. AFTER, same instrument: beat 1 saturation 0.083 -> 0.545 and hue bins 2 -> 5; beat 2 0.083 -> 0.711 and 2 -> 6; beat 4 0.145 -> 0.927. NOT fixed in the engine on purpose: changing viz3d.js:2427 to fall through to the model palette would re-grade all 146 scenes, and the scene-local fix is what every other scene already does. WHY NO EXISTING CHECK CAUGHT IT: acceptance, normals, winding, lumen, check-beat-claims and check-scene-refs all measure the MODEL or the REFS; measure-scene-visibility measures AREA. This defect lives between a correct model and the screen, and nothing in the repo looks there.

ROUND 4, FINDING 2 — CORRECTED BY THIS REVIEW. duod_lumen AND duod_plug CARRIED NO group, SO THE STUDENT'S PARTS LIST FILED THEM UNDER 'Clinical'. viz3d.js:1720 emits a heading only when p.group is truthy AND differs from the previous one, so an ungrouped structure silently inherits whatever heading precedes it. Both are last in structures[], immediately after the three var_* entries whose group is Clinical. VERIFIED IN THE LIVE PLAYER, not from source: I mounted the scene and read the rendered parts list, and it printed 'Clinical :: duod_lumen' and 'Clinical :: duod_plug' beside 'Clinical :: var_malrotation', 'var_highARM' and 'var_hirschsprung'. So a student browsing the part list was told the duodenal lumen and the NORMAL proliferating epithelium are clinical variants — the exact opposite of beat 8's teaching, which is that the plug is a normal stage that must resolve. Both now carry group 'Foregut', the duodenum's group; re-probed in the player and they now print under Foregut. Nothing in the repo checks that a structure has a group.

ROUND 4, FINDING 3 — OPEN, NOT FIXABLE BY ME, AND IT INVALIDATES A PROOF EVERY ROUND HAS QUOTED. BEAT 9'S walk-scene-in-player RESULT IS NONDETERMINISTIC. Same bytes, same tool, same container, three full walks: run 1 reported beat 9 healthy at 18%x12% with 0 clipped; runs 2 and 3 reported 'beat 9 CLIPPED — 164 SUBJECT px on the frame border', identical count both times. Run 2 was the UNMODIFIED scene, so this is not my correction — I re-ran the original bytes specifically to attribute it. Walking beat 9 ALONE (--beats 9) never clips and reports 24%x16%, three times out of three. THE VARIABLE IS TRACE_STRUCTURE: beat 9 carries one, the harness's own header says the frame it measures is 'the trace's last waypoint, which is where the player parks it', and where that lands depends on what ran before it. CONSEQUENCE: every 'walk-scene-in-player ... 0 clipped' in this item's history — the round-3 build run's proof, and round 3's own review — is a coin flip, not a measurement, and the beat that carries the scene's central mechanism (the 270-degree rotation) really does run off the frame edge about two times in three. WHY I DID NOT FIX IT: the candidate fixes are (a) drop TRACE_STRUCTURE from beat 9, which deletes teaching, (b) give beat 9 an explicit framing or camera op after the trace so the parked camera is not the measured one, or (c) make the player park deterministically. (b) is probably right and is a build change; (c) is an engine change. Choosing between them is the build task's call, not a reviewer's unilateral edit to a beat that is otherwise correct. WHAT TO VERIFY WHEN FIXED: run the FULL walk three times and require beat 9 to report the same span and 0 clipped each time. A single clean walk proves nothing here, which is the real lesson.

ROUND 4, STANDARDS GAPS PROPOSED (REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT section 4). (1) NOTHING CHECKS THAT A STRUCTURE'S COLOUR SURVIVES TO THE SCREEN. The mechanical review already forbids 'reimplementing winding, normals, colour ... locally instead of using render-kit.js' — that checks the MODEL's colour and this scene passed it while rendering monochrome, because the loss happens in the player. Proposed, and it is one pass over the corpus: fail any 3d_anatomy scene with a structure that has no color AND whose model exposes a LAYERS entry for its part, since that combination is exactly the viz3d.js:2427 fallback. A cheaper version catches it from the other end: assert a walked beat is not monochrome (occupied hue bins > 1, or median saturation above a floor). Either would have caught this at source and neither exists. (2) NOTHING CHECKS THAT A STRUCTURE HAS A group. An ungrouped structure does not error — it is silently filed under the preceding heading, which makes the damage depend on array ORDER, so the same omission is harmless in one position and teaches a falsehood in another. Proposed: validate-scenes should require a group on every role 'part' structure. (3) A PROOF THAT IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE SHOULD NOT COUNT AS A PROOF. Finding 3 is a tool reporting two different verdicts on identical bytes, and every round so far has quoted its single run as settled. Proposed, for ARTWORK-STANDARD section 3 and the build prompt: any harness whose result depends on animation timing — today that is every beat carrying TRACE_STRUCTURE — must be run at least twice and AGREE before its result is quoted, and a run that quotes it says how many times it ran. (4) THE CONSECUTIVE-FRAMES RULE DOES NOT COVER THE PAIR THAT MOST NEEDS IT. Mechanical review requires that no view render the same frame as the view BEFORE it. The pair at real risk of being two identical pictures is a VARIANT and its normal twin, which are typically many beats apart — here beat 12 (normal partition) and beat 18 (high ARM) are six apart and are the lowest-differing pair in the whole scene at 2.99%. They do differ, legibly and correctly, so this is a proposal and not a finding. Proposed: extend the rule to compare every declared variant against the beat its own narration names as the comparison.

ROUND 4 — WHAT IS RIGHT, so round 5 does not re-litigate it. ALL THREE ROUND-3 FINDINGS ARE GENUINELY CLOSED, checked against the scene and the player rather than from built_notes. R3F1 (beat 11 cut nothing): cloaca is now role 'context' and the player really does clip it; the interior is still not legible at that scale, but that is measured, DECLARED in gaps[] entry 21, and beat 12 is the compensating close-up — closed with an honest declaration rather than a green number. R3F2 (five wrong beat pointers): I re-resolved all seven myself against the 18-beat scene. Beat 4 -> 3 (both t=0.3), beat 6's 'next beat but one' -> beat 8 (the cord beat was inserted exactly there), beat 7 -> 17 (beat 17's list does open with oesophageal atresia), beat 9 -> 17, beat 10 -> 9, beat 16 -> 17, beat 18 -> 12. All seven land, and beat_refs records each one. R3F3 (solid cord had no picture): beat 8 exists, duod_plug is pinned @0.52, and the cord is unmistakable in the render. MY OWN THREE CHECKS, chosen from the scene and the curriculum entry before using built_notes as a checklist, all PASS. (i) ISOLATE_REGION targets: the scene mixes group names ('Blood supply', 'The two boundaries', 'Hindgut', 'Innervation') with raw structure keys ('duodenum', 'respir', 'caecum', 'var_highARM'), and if either kind failed to resolve the close-up framing — the entire fix for rounds 2 and 3 — would silently do nothing. viz3d's keysFor() resolves BOTH, and I confirmed all ten targets resolve to a non-empty key set. Clean. (ii) THE STAGE_LIMITED RULE THE ROUND-3 BUILD RUN DISCOVERED, applied exhaustively rather than to the three cases it found: of the nine STAGE_LIMITED structures, exactly three are absent at t=1 (buccoph, cloacalmem, duod_plug) and therefore could never be drawn by an unpinned ref — and all three are pinned. urorectal, anorectal, urogenital, enteric, appendix and duod_lumen are all present at t=1 and correctly unpinned. The fix was complete. (iii) The papilla's side at beat 1's instant, which no acceptance row covers: measured on mesh vertices at t = 0, 0.08, 0.15 and 0.2 the papilla is at x = 0.0000, dead on the midline, which is right for a straight pre-rotation tube, and it is on the embryo's RIGHT at every t from 0.3 on. Beat 4's 'the upper one is the papilla, the lower one is the watershed' holds at its own t=0.3. The two beads DO invert by t=1 (watershed y +0.161 against papilla y +0.001) — that is the rotation and fixation doing real work, beat 14's closing sentence says so in as many words, and it is not a defect. THE WAIVERS HOLD: all 19 either name a beat that shows the structure or argue why no closer framing could carry the beat, and I checked the four that my first pass flagged — my flag was a bad regex, 'beats 3, 4, 6 and 7' does not match 'beat <digit>'. Reporting my own false positive because the next run should not re-raise it. THE NARRATION IS MEDICALLY SOUND and I checked it as an examiner: T12/L1/L3 artery levels, papilla in D2, watershed at the 2/3 point of the transverse colon, greater/lesser/least splanchnic T5-T9 / T10-T11 / T12 with epigastric / periumbilical / suprapubic referral, hindgut to the pectinate line, ventral pancreatic bud the smaller one that swings round, trachea in front and oesophagus behind, 90 degrees then 180 more anticlockwise about the SMA, duodenal atresia as a recanalization failure against jejunoileal atresia which is not, Hirschsprung always involving the rectum because it is colonised last. No error found. MECHANICAL REVIEW PASSES, re-run by me: validate-scenes 146/146 after my edit; check-proof-matches-scene 84 against 84, THE PROOF WAS RUN AGAINST THE SCENE ON DISK; the real player walks all 18 beats with a clean console apart from swiftshader's GPU-stall warnings; no two CONSECUTIVE beats render the same frame, smallest consecutive difference 4.27% (beats 16-17). ONE THING I CONSIDERED AND DELIBERATELY DID NOT RAISE: in beat 12 the anorectal canal and urogenital sinus are ghosted to 0.10 while only the septum is highlighted, so the two chambers the beat teaches are the dimmest things in it. After the colour fix they are distinguishable (dark purple against light), and the player draws pins and labels that the walk harness's canvas capture does not include — so judging legibility from these PNGs alone would be blaming the instrument, which is the error round 3 correctly rejected. Recorded so it is not re-derived blind.

ROUND 2 REWORK - BOTH R1 FINDINGS ADDRESSED; full account in BUILD-LOG.md under 2026-10-01 '19:05Z slot'. (1) FINDING 1 IS FIXED IN THE MODEL AND THE SCENE IS UNTOUCHED - byte-identical to what was committed, checked rather than assumed. The review proposed ROTATE_TO_VIEW superior; I built it and LOOKED, and it is worse: ISOLATE_REGION frames on the blocked sperm, so the superior camera leaves the shell it rests on out of frame (zona 45.3% -> 0.688% of frame) and the beat FAILS on granule_exudate. A beat about a sperm resting on a shell cannot be fixed by a camera that loses the shell. So I measured the finding's actual question in pixels - render the head's silhouette and the ooplasm disc at beat 6's own camera and intersect them - and the committed seat puts 46.1% of the head INSIDE the interior. Swept 7 seats; adopted bd=(0.86,-0.46,0.22): 0.0% inside, 17.7% zona still in frame, head unobstructed. The review's own (0.78,-0.58,0.22) also measures 0.0% but leaves less shell (16.4%) and puts a corona cell across the head. THE STAND-OFF STAYED SOLVED: the model reads zonaOut() in whatever direction it is given, so row C re-measures and comes back -0.060 - it still rests on the surface and does not penetrate. (2) FINDING 2 DIAGNOSED, AND THE REVIEW'S HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG. The id-pick pass replaces materials with an OPAQUE MeshBasicMaterial, dropping the scene's own per-structure opacity, so the outermost shell swallows everything behind it. PROVED BY ARITHMETIC: sum(pct) equals subject_pct to within rounding in ALL NINE beats (beat 7: zona 80.558 + perivitelline 19.442 = 100.000, six structures inside them at exactly 0). It is NOT the pinned-t hypothesis the review offered: mount() uses the same groupFor() for both passes, and beat 9 reads sperm_head 0.678 / oocyte_chromatin 0.670 / centriole 0.311 at the SAME pins that read 0 in beat 8, because nothing translucent stands in front of them there. Enclosure is the variable, not pinning. (3) THE VERDICTS WERE RIGHT, SO NOTHING IN THE PASS/FAIL EXPRESSION MOVED. The alpha fallback already carried every zero at peaks 54-155 against the 40/255 floor, and I checked it cannot be fooled by a secondary effect: standardLights() casts no shadows and shadowMap is off, so hiding a structure changes only its own pixels. The fix is evidentiary: visible_pct (ink with only OPAQUE structures occluding) and witness (which measure cleared each pointed-at structure, and by how much) are reported and printed; seen() is byte-for-byte unchanged. NO SILENT RE-GRADING, MEASURED NOT ASSERTED: patched tool vs unpatched on the same scene returns byte-identical pct, subject_pct and verdict on 8 of 9 beats - all but the one whose model changed. The two measures cross-check: beat 4 zona_channel 20.613/20.613, beat 8 sperm_head 3.405/3.401. (4) A SECOND HOLE FOUND AND DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN FOR A REVIEWER TO RULE ON: idPointBad filters on r.pct[k]!=null and pct only carries VISIBLE keys, so a beat that HIGHLIGHTs a structure it has HIDDEN is never even looked at. No beat here does it. Now reported as pointed_but_hidden and printed, but NOT failed, because failing it would re-grade other scenes mid-flight. Same reason visible_pct was not promoted to primary, which it probably should be in a deliberate corpus-wide pass. (5) PROVED: acceptance 27/27 with a magnitude floor and a rejecting negative case each; winding 1472/1472 outward, 0 reversed; signed volume positive and winding-by-area 1 for every in-domain part at four t; console clean apart from 4 swiftshader driver messages filtered by exact pattern and printed; 65/65 (structure,beat) pairs resolve with geometry through the REAL viz3d adapter at each beat's own t; check-beat-claims 40 claims 0 failures 0 beats unpinned; measure-scene-visibility 9 beats 0 failures 6 waivers, now witnessed; 3 solved parameters perturbed and all three move; 0 undeclared interpenetrations. validate-scenes is 1/1 NOT 146/146 - only one scene was staged into this container, and saying so is the point. (6) A REGRESSION I AM DECLARING RATHER THAN HIDING: walk-scene-in-player reports beat 6 CLIPPED at 623 subject px on the frame border against 307 before my change. Pre-existing - beats 4, 5 and 9 clip too and I touched none of them - but mine on beat 6. I checked whether the other seat was kinder and it is not: the review's seat clips at 605. The clipping is the price of swinging the sperm toward the silhouette at all, not a bad choice between candidates; the real question is frame padding in the player's per-view refit, which affects four beats here and other scenes besides. (7) COST: the tool now does one extra render and read-back per visible structure per beat - this walk went from ~90s to ~4min on swiftshader. Worth knowing before running it on a 51-structure scene. (8) SECTION 6: I did NOT test the shell on Frank's machine - the prompt and BUILD-TASK-PROMPT section 0 both say it is dead and tell the run not to try, and I followed that. I am the EIGHTH run to raise it; the seven before me tested it and found node v22.23.2 working. I add no new evidence, but a standing instruction seven runs have contradicted and none can get corrected is itself the finding, and it costs us the real lock on the real queue file.

READ-BACK (section 3), by re-staging every file and comparing sha256 against the copy this run built. 39 files committed in three calls, 0 rejected, every expectedMtimeMs guard held. MATCHING EXACTLY: models3d/fertilization.js 118398 B c89978ea3128be60; viz-training/tools/measure-scene-visibility.mjs 41596 B 2cc67e1ce558f5c9; BUILD-LOG.md 1308803 B 727f40fa632b24ac; BUILD-QUEUE.json 831787 B 567b81259edbfcf6; player/visibility.json 15610 B 5c79d6ae7562701b; report.json 52404 B 11189f41c761d8cd. All mtimes later than this run's start (19:05:47Z). AND THE SCENE IS PROVED UNTOUCHED AT THE DEVICE LEVEL: the scene JSON re-stages at mtime 1790879220020, identical to what it carried when this run first staged it at 19:06Z - nothing wrote to it, which is the strong form of 'the scene needed no change'. || THE PNGS DO NOT MATCH BY WHOLE-FILE SHA AND IT IS NOT A FAILED COMMIT - A PROPERTY OF THE COMMIT PATH NOBODY HAS RECORDED. beat06.png shipped 181032 B and reads back 186802 B; cell-t060.png shipped 359258 B and reads back 365028 B - THE SAME DELTA BOTH TIMES, exactly 5770 bytes, which is not what corruption looks like. Took them apart chunk by chunk: PNG signature identical, IHDR identical, CONCATENATED IDAT BYTE-IDENTICAL (180435 B sha fd19a7655b75bc84 and 358145 B sha 1bcc5f26515b840b) - the pixels are exactly the pixels I rendered. The difference is one extra ancillary chunk on disk in both, caBX of 5758 B inserted after IHDR (5758 + 12 of chunk framing = 5770); caBX is where C2PA content-provenance manifests live. So device_commit_files injects a provenance manifest into every PNG it writes. It is ancillary and outside the image stream, so no renderer or reviewer sees it. THIS MATTERS FOR THE PROTOCOL: section 3 says read your files back, and the 18:34Z round did it by sha256 calling that 'stronger than mtime alone' - which it is, for TEXT. For a PNG a whole-file sha256 WILL ALWAYS MISMATCH, for every run that has ever committed a proof render, and a run applying the text rule to an image would conclude its commit did not land when it did - then either report RUN FAILED and leave the item, or force the write past a guard that was never failing. The right read-back for a PNG is IHDR plus the concatenated IDAT, and BUILD-TASK-PROMPT section 3 should say so. I did not edit that file: it is the standing instruction for all three tasks and is not one item's rework to change.

A SECOND PROPERTY OF THE COMMIT PATH, FOUND BY THE READ-BACK ITSELF AND WORTH MORE THAN THIS ITEM. A device_commit_files call REPORTED written AND DID NOT CHANGE THE FILE. This run appended to BUILD-LOG.md twice. The first landed. The second was committed from the SAME stagedPath the first had used, came back in the written array with nothing in rejected, moved the file's mtime on the device - and left the CONTENT at the previous append's 1308803 bytes instead of the 1311911 I had staged. BUILD-QUEUE.json, committed in the same call from an equivalently reused path, landed correctly, so this is not a blanket failure of the call. THE READ-BACK IS THE ONLY REASON I KNOW: written was a lie, rejected was empty, the mtime moved, and every signal short of comparing the bytes said it had succeeded. That is precisely the failure BUILD-TASK-PROMPT section 3 exists for - 'a commit that was issued is not a commit that landed' - and section 3's note that reading back is STRICTLY STRONGER than trusting the written/rejected arrays is now demonstrated rather than argued. Working hypothesis: the transfer layer keys a cache on the staged path, so re-committing a CHANGED file from a path already used this session can serve the earlier blob. THE FIX A RUN CAN APPLY TODAY: commit each revision from a FRESH stagedPath - which is what the successful retry used - and read back by CONTENT every time. Final state verified: BUILD-LOG.md 1313298 B sha b43de9c66bc634f1 on disk, matching what was shipped.
findings: BEAT 6 TEACHES THE OPPOSITE OF ITS NARRATION. Beat 6 ('it rests on the hardened shell and gets no further') is ROTATE_TO_VIEW anterior. The geometry is right -- blocked_sperm's apex stands at 7.663 against a zona outer surface of 7.603 at t=0.6, and acceptance row C passes because it measures 3-D radius. But at the anterior camera (0,0,1) the direction bd=(0.62,-0.46,0.64) gives a screen-plane factor sin=0.770, so the head projects to screen radius 5.90-6.28 against an ooplasm disc at 6.00 and the zona inner surface at 6.20: its apex projects INSIDE the zona's inner edge, and with bd_z positive it sits between camera and oocyte and occludes the shell. The student sees the second sperm inside the cell in the one beat whose point is that it cannot get in. FIX: ROTATE_TO_VIEW superior (0,1,0.001), sin=0.889, projects 6.81-7.25, clear of both -- then RE-RENDER and look, which is why this was not hand-applied (no chromium on the device). Alternative if superior composes badly: swing bd toward the silhouette, e.g. (0.78,-0.58,0.22), sin=0.975, but that moves row C's input. NOTE models3d/fertilization.js:1304 screenSeparation() already does exactly this projection and is called only once, at :1500, on sperm_head vs oocyte_chromatin.

THE VISIBILITY WALK PASSES BEATS WHOSE SUBJECTS IT CANNOT SEE. In player/visibility.json, 4 of 9 beats have a POINTED-AT structure measuring exactly 0% ink while the walk reports unseeable:[] and pointedBad:[] -- beat 4 (inner_acrosomal_membrane, zona_channel, oolemma), beat 5 (depolarisation_wave, cortical_granules, oolemma), beat 7 (second_polar_body, mii_spindle), beat 8 (sperm_head, oocyte_chromatin). So '9/9 beats pass the visibility walk' is not witnessed by its own artifact. THE PICTURES ARE FINE -- I looked at beats 7 and 8 and the subjects dominate both frames -- so this is an INSTRUMENT defect, not a scene defect, and the scene should NOT be changed for it. But the visibility evidence for this scene currently proves nothing and the same blind instrument is passing every model3d scene in the corpus. Hypothesis, not a finding: most zero-ink keys are the ones gaps[] declares PINNED to their beat's own t, so the ink pass may build at the view's t while the beauty pass honours the pin; oolemma, sperm_head and oocyte_chromatin are not pinned and are not explained by that.

ESCALATED, reason 3. BEAT 6'S NARRATION TEACHES THE OPPOSITE OF BEAT 6'S PICTURE. The title ('The second sperm has nothing left to use'), the ops, the SHOW_RELATIONSHIP ('it rests on the hardened shell and gets no further') and claim B6-blocked-out (penetration atMost 0, measured -0.060) all assert the polyspermy block HELD, and beat06.png agrees: the sperm lies flat and outside an intact zona. The narration on that same frame is, in full: 'Both fail and you get dispermy - a triploid conceptus, usually 69,XXY, which is not viable and is the classic origin of a partial mole.' So the student is shown the block WORKING and told what happens when it FAILS. Two harms: (1) 'Both' has no antecedent on screen - the two blocks are named in beat 5's narration, a different frame; (2) the natural reading of that sentence over that picture is that the pictured event IS dispermy, so a student can leave beat 6 believing a sperm stuck on the zona produces a triploid conceptus. There is no dispermy geometry anywhere in the scene to correct the reading. IT IS A DECISION, NOT A DEFECT, which is why it is escalated and not sent back: the fix needs either new narration for beat 6 (forbidden by the scene's own declared rule, carried from this item's note, that no narration was edited, shortened or rewritten) or new dispermy geometry (forbidden to the review task by section 5, and a widening of the scene's teaching scope a build task should not choose alone). A fourth round can only pick one and present it as done. Created by the 5/6 narration split, and INVISIBLE TO EVERY GATE: the build run proved the split reassembles byte-identically with no word lost, which is true, and is exactly what left a conditional about failure sitting on a frame showing success.

FIXED BY THIS RUN, no action needed. BEAT 4 TAUGHT THE WRONG FUSION MEMBRANE. Three places said the INNER ACROSOMAL MEMBRANE is the surface that fuses with the oolemma: the B4-iam claim gloss, the SHOW_RELATIONSHIP kind from inner_acrosomal_membrane to oolemma, and the inner_acrosomal_membrane narration. It is not. The IAM is the leading face that penetrates the zona; fusion is between the oolemma and the sperm's PLASMA membrane over the EQUATORIAL (post-acrosomal) segment, where IZUMO1 is localised. Examined directly; a student taught by beat 4 loses the mark. The scene ALREADY HAD IT RIGHT in its own oolemma structure (terms[] list 'equatorial segment' and 'IZUMO1', narration carried verbatim) - so the scene contradicted itself and the WRONG version was the one highlighted, labelled and machine-checked, while the right one sat in a structure the beat does not point at. Corrected in all three; provenance.corrected_at/corrected_by/correction_note set. No geometry changed and no re-render needed (grep of models3d/fertilization.js finds none of the three phrasings - the model never asserted it). No measure changed: B4-iam still measures acrosome.iamExposed equals true and still passes, which is exactly why every gate passed with the error in place. No carried narration touched: of the three texts only one is narration and it is build-task-authored, carrying no narration_from. Re-ran after: validate-scenes 146/146, check-beat-claims 40 claims 0 failures.

STANDARDS GAP (section 4), the one that matters beyond this item. The beat 6 defect passes EVERY gate in ARTWORK-STANDARD section 3 Review 1, and passed round 1. Structurally: every mechanical gate checks GEOMETRY against CLAIMS and NOT ONE checks NARRATION against the claims, title or ops of its own beat. A scene can machine-prove a sperm did not get in while telling the student both blocks failed, and score 40/40. PROPOSED: add a narration/claim polarity check - a beat whose claims assert an event did NOT happen must not carry narration whose subject is that event happening; and flag every beat whose narration arrived by SPLITTING another beat's, for a human read of each half alone on its own frame. The cheap first version is just the flag, and it would have caught this.

SECOND STANDARDS GAP, hit by this run. REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT section 2 says to decide your own three checks BEFORE reading the builder's notes. That is structurally impossible as written: built_notes live inside the queue item and section 1 tells you to open BUILD-QUEUE.json first to find the item. I had read ~9,000 words of the builder's account before I could have formed an independent order. PROPOSED: give queue-set.mjs --show a flag that prints status/built_at/review_rounds WITHOUT built_notes, or have section 1 say to read only those fields first. (My three checks, written before touching the model and recorded in BUILD-LOG.md: beat 6 narration vs picture; which membrane beat 4 says fuses; beat 8's 'twenty-three chromosomes' vs the declared five-per-set drawing. Two of the three found defects; the third came back clean and is recorded so a later round does not re-raise it.)

ROOT CAUSE, CONFIRMED IN viz3d.js, AND IT IS A SCENE DEFECT RATHER THAN AN ENGINE ONE: the ops run in order, ISOLATE_REGION 'Cut open' sets state.only to the five cut keys (line 1906), then COMPARE_STRUCTURES ['icm_cut','mural_troph_cut'] OVERWRITES state.only with just those two (lines 1913-1916). subjectBox() frames on state.only (line 2127) and its own comment says ghosted context 'is allowed to run off the edges'. polar_troph_cut is not in the compare pair, so the engine is doing exactly what it documents, and the beat asked it to frame on a pair that excludes the cap. The same mechanism explains beat 5's outlier framing — it compares the two pole markers, which bracket the embryo, so its box_fill is 6.54% against 75.4% in every other cut beat. WHY A STUDENT LOSES MARKS: B4-cap-seals-the-mass is phrased as a claim about what is SEEN — 'the thicker wall covers the whole of the mass's footprint, with no blue showing past the darker red' — and it is asserted at tol 1e-9 in the model's own frame while the apex of that cap is off-screen. The claim is true of the geometry and unviewable in the frame that carries it, which is RENDER-STANDARD 3.y's shape exactly. FIX, scene-side and one line: put polar_troph_cut into beat 4's COMPARE_STRUCTURES targets, or drop the COMPARE op (the beat already highlights icm_cut and carries a SHOW_RELATIONSHIP to polar_troph_cut). Then re-run the walk and confirm no subject pixel lies on a border row or column.

ROUND 3 · STANDARDS GAP BEHIND F1, per REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT section 4. RENDER-STANDARD section 3 says 'THE SUBJECT FILLS THE FRAME, AT EVERY t. A camera parked at a distance that suited one stage will CROP another and SHRINK a third.' The standard names both directions; the tool implements one. tools/measure-scene-visibility.mjs line 583 computes framing = r.subject_pct < MIN_SUBJECT, so it fires only when the subject is too SMALL. Worse, boxFillPct (line 403) CLAMPS the projected bounding box to the frame with Math.min(1,x1) - Math.max(-1,x0), so whatever overflows is discarded BEFORE the number is formed: beat 4 reports the HIGHEST box_fill in the scene, 85.05%, and framing:false, on the one frame that is clipped. The single number that could have revealed the overflow is the one that throws the information away. PROPOSED RULE: 'THE SUBJECT IS INSIDE THE FRAME, NOT MERELY BIG ENOUGH IN IT. The visibility walk asserts that no pixel of the subject lies on a border row or column, and reports the UNCLAMPED projected extent of the subject box, so an overflow shows as a number greater than 1 instead of being clamped to it. A beat that must crop carries a framing waiver saying what is cut and why.' CORPUS SCOPE: embryology__week-3-gastrulation__primitive-streak declares the same symptom in its own gaps[] (beats 7 and 10 clip the disc; engine-side fix engine__refit-camera-on-isolate, which is ESCALATED). Blastocyst has the same symptom from a different op and declares nothing — and that difference, not the crop, is what the rule would remove.

BEAT 9'S VISIBILITY WAIVER IS ACCEPTED, and I checked its escape hatch rather than its argument: the waiver's defence is that beat 5 shows the cap face-on, and beat 5 does — the polar cap is a plainly legible pale salmon band across the top of the embryo there, so the two-claims-two-cameras argument RENDER-STANDARD 3.y permits is actually discharged and not merely asserted.

ROUND 4 · F5 · THE EXPANSION — THE ONE THING THIS MODEL IS BUILT AROUND — IS INVISIBLE ACROSS THE WALK, AND BEAT 8 NARRATES A SIZE RATIO THE FRAMES CONTRADICT. viz3d's frameView() calls subjectBox() then distanceForBox() on EVERY view (viz3d.js lines 2127-2171), so the camera is refitted to whatever that beat shows and every beat is normalised to the same fill. Measured on the shipped round-4 walk: beats 2, 3, 4 and 6 have the IDENTICAL subject bounding box, 115,21..984,878, and box_fill_pct 75.40 on all four — at t = 0.18, 0.42, 0.52 and 0.86, where the model's own battery (models-out/blastocyst/proof.json, perT) gives embryoD_um 122.08, 143.77, 157.40 and ~193.5. The embryo grows by a factor of 1.60 across those four beats and is drawn the same size to the pixel. WHERE IT COSTS A STUDENT MARKS: beat 1 (t = 0, D = 120.00 um, morula in its zona) renders at bbox 223,129..876,770 — 653 x 641 px, subject 33.37%, box_fill 75.40 — and beat 8 (t = 0.78, D = 190.86 um, bare blastocyst) renders at 224,130..875,769 — 651 x 639 px, subject 33.33%, box_fill 75.40. Beat 8's narration is "a bare blastocyst about 190 um across — half again the width of the morula that entered the uterus, and not one cell has grown to do it", and beat 7 carries B7-expanded (embryoDRel atLeast 1.4) as a machine-checked claim. The student is told "half again the width", shown the morula, then shown the blastocyst at 99.7% of the morula's on-screen width. The claim is true of the geometry and false of every picture that carries it — RENDER-STANDARD 3.y's shape again, which is also what round 3's F1 was. THIS IS NOT THE ESCALATED ENGINE ITEM. engine__refit-camera-on-isolate is about WHICH keys form the subject box (state.only being overwritten); this is about the DISTANCE being recomputed per beat at all, which happens on every view in the corpus whether or not it isolates. Confirmed there is no scene-side fix: frameView takes no scene input, there is no SET_CAMERA or distance op, and camera.framing/framing_strict only choose the DIRECTION. PROPOSED FIX, for whoever takes it: a scene-declarable scale group — a set of beats that share one camera distance, computed once from the LARGEST subject box in the group — so beats 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 hold one scale and the growth is the thing the walk shows. Cheaper interim, scene-side and available today: beat 8's size sentence is the only one that states a ratio, so if the scale group is not built, that clause should be re-attributed to the structure's own text where no frame is implied by it. SEVERITY: this is the scene's declared subject. gaps[] says "ONE input function of t (pumped fluid volume)" and the learning_goal ends "and date days five to six correctly"; the walk currently shows the wall thinning and the cavity filling, and never shows the embryo getting bigger.

ROUND 4 · STANDARDS GAP BEHIND F5, per REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT section 4. RENDER-STANDARD section 3 line 124 reads "THE SUBJECT FILLS THE FRAME, AT EVERY t. A parametric model changes size and position as t advances. A camera parked at a distance that suited one stage will crop another and shrink a third. Fit to the bounding box every rebuild — VizKit.fitCamera." The rule is unqualified, and for a model whose single input IS growth it mandates the defect: refitting every beat guarantees that the quantity the model solves for can never appear on screen. The standard names only the failure of a FIXED camera and not the failure of a refitted one. PROPOSED RULE, to sit beside it: "A FIT IS PER SCENE-GROUP, NOT PER BEAT. Where beats differ in a size the narration or a claim compares, they share one camera distance, fitted to the largest subject among them, and the walk reports the on-screen extent of each so an unintended normalisation shows as a flat series. A beat that must be refitted alone says so." CORPUS SCOPE, not just this scene: every parametric process scene is exposed — embryology__gametogenesis-fertilization__cleavage-morula holds the same cell-volume invariant and narrates the same journey, and the folding and heart-tube scenes all narrate growth. This was invisible to every tool because measure-scene-visibility reports subject_pct and box_fill_pct, which are both RATIOS TO THE FRAME: after a refit they are constant by construction, so the one number that would have shown it — the subject's real size against its on-screen size — is not computed anywhere. Round 3 added the unclamped extent and the border-pixel count to that tool; this wants a third column, um-per-pixel, and it is one line next to the others.

At the implantation site — which is the polar surface, not this one — ...". F3 (the cavity read as a solid ball): closed in the picture, which is the only place it could be closed. In beats 3, 4, 5 and 6 it draws as one saturated blue mound apposed to the inner face of the polar trophoblast and bulging into the cavity, at a single pole, with the thicker cap sitting over exactly its footprint; an examiner asking a student to identify the inner cell mass on any of those frames would mark it right, and nothing in the frame offers a competing candidate. The non-radial partition with a two-piece cavity that the build offered as the honest next step is NOT needed; do not spend a round on it. ROUND 4 · CORRECTED IN-ROUND, BOTH IN THE SCENE, recorded here because provenance alone is not where the next run looks. (1) BEAT 10 TOLD THE STUDENT THE EMBRYO HAD NOT HATCHED WHILE ITS OWN CLAIM AND ITS OWN PICTURE SAID IT WAS 84% OUT OF THE SHELL — and the false sentence was ADDED BY ROUND 4 ITSELF, closing F4. The added text read "The zona is back because the embryo has not hatched yet". Beat 10 stands at t = 0.72; the model has T_HATCH0 = 0.60 and T_HATCH1 = 0.78 with aperture = pi * smoothstep, so zonaCoverFrac = (1 + cos(pi * 0.7407)) / 2 = 0.1569 — I re-derived this from the constants rather than taking the figure from gaps[], and player/beat10.png shows it: a khaki crescent over the top third of an otherwise bare embryo. The beat's OWN machine-checked claim B10-zona-open asserts zonaCoverFrac atMost 0.45 with the words "the zona is already breaking", so the prose and the claim on one beat said opposite things, on the scene whose learning_goal is why the embryo must hatch before it can implant. Corrected to "has not FINISHED hatching — it is thinned and already breached, and the blastocyst is still inside it", which is true of t = 0.72, agrees with B10-zona-open and B10-zona-thin and with the beat's later sentence about thinning the zona artificially, and keeps the step back from beat 9 that F4 asked for. NOTE FOR THE STANDARD: nothing in the battery, the 51 beat claims or the visibility walk compares a beat's PROSE against the beat's own CLAIMS, which is why a sentence could be added that its neighbour in the same object contradicts. That check is cheap and this is the second round running in which the narration, not the geometry, carried the defect. (2) BEAT 6'S VIEW NARRATION HAD A BROKEN SPLICE from round 4's F2 rework — "and that is the whole of it. and it is the half of the trophoblast" — a sentence starting lowercase after a full stop, in student-facing text. Capitalised; no wording changed, nothing deleted.

ROUND 5 · R1 · THE FIX FOR F5 OVER-REACHED AND DELETED A TRUE, UNCONTRADICTED, EXAMINABLE SENTENCE ALONG WITH THE FALSE ONE. CORRECTED IN-ROUND. Closing F5 the build removed from beat 8 the whole clause "— half again the width of the morula that entered the uterus, and not one cell has grown to do it". Only the first half is a ratio between two beats and only the first half is contradicted by the frames. "Not one cell has grown to do it" states no ratio; it is asserted ON THIS BEAT by its own machine-checked claim B8-cells (cellVolRel near 1, tol 0.004); the zygote it compares against is not drawn anywhere in this scene, so no frame can contradict it. The build's OWN written rule in the same note — "an ABSOLUTE size is not affected and stays ... only a RATIO is contradicted" — applies to it and was not applied to it. HOW I KNOW IT MATTERED, measured across the whole file before correcting: after round 5 NO view narration anywhere in this scene told a student that the expansion costs no cytoplasm. I grepped all ten beats; the fact survived only in four CLAIM strings (B1-cells, B2-no-growth, B6-cells, B8-cells) and in structures[blastocoele]. That the embryo grows by half again with no increase in cytoplasm is the single most examinable thing about blastocyst expansion, and round 5 removed it from the student-facing walk as collateral while fixing an unrelated defect. CORRECTED: beat 8 now reads "... about 190 µm across, holding the same quantity of cytoplasm as the zygote did — not one cell has grown." Both clauses map exactly onto claims carried by this beat (B8-size, B8-cells) and neither states a ratio between beats, so F5 does not reopen. A first version of my own correction ended "; what has been added is fluid" and I cut it before committing: beat 8 draws the blastocyst from OUTSIDE and does not draw the cavity, and this beat's own narration_from states the rule "A beat must not narrate what it does not draw".

ROUND 5 · R2 AND R3 · TWO SMALLER DEFECTS ROUND 5 INTRODUCED, BOTH CORRECTED IN-ROUND, BOTH PROSE. (R2) CLAIM B8-cells' TEXT WAS A FRAGMENT LEFT BEHIND BY THE EXCISION: it read "and the same quantity of cytoplasm as the zygote" — a sentence-initial "and" that had grammatically continued the clause round 5 deleted. Leading "and" removed; measure, op, value and tol untouched. This is the SECOND ROUND RUNNING in which a text edit left a dangling fragment in student-facing or student-visible text — round 4 corrected beat 6's "and that is the whole of it. and it is the half of the trophoblast" from its own F2 rework. (R3) THE TWO STRUCTURES THAT RECEIVED THE MOVED CLAUSE DID NOT RECORD RECEIVING IT. structures[blastocoele].narration_from still read 'sequence-version structure "blastocoele" — carried across verbatim' and structures[blastocoele_cut].narration_from mentioned only the sectioning, although round 5 APPENDED a sentence to both. The build note states "narration_from and gaps[27] record it": the narration_from that records it is VIEW 8's, not either of the two structures the text was moved INTO, and gaps has 27 entries so its last index is [26], not [27] — the entry is real, the citation is off by one. This matters beyond bookkeeping because THIS FILE'S OWN gaps[22] is round 4's finding that a narration marked verbatim on both halves of a split structure can be false of one of them; a reader who trusts "carried across verbatim" would take a round-5 transplant for SVG-era text. Both narration_from fields now record the move, why it was made, and where to read the rest (view 8, gaps[26], engine__camera-scale-group).

ROUND 5 · CONVERGENCE AND STATUS. Round 5 STARTED with 1 open finding (round 4's F5) and ENDS WITH 0. F5 is closed — half on the scene by the interim round 4 sanctioned in writing, half by escalation to engine__camera-scale-group, which round 4 also instructed in writing. Three defects round 5 introduced were found by this review and ALL THREE CORRECTED IN-ROUND, so none is carried. Open counts by round: 4 -> 2 -> 4 -> 1 -> 0. Falling; the progress rule does not fire; not escalated. SET TO done. WHAT I ACCEPT, SAID PLAINLY RATHER THAN LEFT IN A GAP: this scene teaches the embryo's expansion in words and does not show it. A student walking the ten beats sees the wall thin and the cavity fill and never sees the embryo get bigger, because the player refits the camera per beat. That is a real reduction against the learning_goal, it is declared in gaps[26], no sentence a student reads is contradicted by the frame carrying it, and the capability that would fix it is filed and escalated. I would put this in front of a student in that state; I would not have, with a sentence on screen that the picture under it disproved. THE SCENE STAYS AT status candidate AND I DID NOT PROMOTE IT. gaps[1] says 'Only a review that did not build this promotes it (ARTWORK-STANDARD)' — I am that review, and I went to ARTWORK-STANDARD to do it. THE RULE IS NOT THERE. ARTWORK-STANDARD has no candidate/ready transition anywhere in it; its sections 3-5 define the two reviews, the first plate's cost and the per-plate log, and nothing about scene status. So the gap cites an authority that does not carry the rule, and inventing the transition myself would be a decision rather than a correction. FOR WHOEVER OWNS THE STANDARDS (section 4): either write the candidate -> ready rule into ARTWORK-STANDARD with its conditions, or correct gaps[1] to name whatever document actually holds it. Until then no scene in this corpus can be promoted by anyone following its own instructions, which is a silent stall of exactly the kind section 0 is about.

built_notes:
CONVERTED, NOT WIRED. The sequence-version scene had 15 teaching panels and no geometry; it is now a
3d_anatomy scene of 30 structures and 10 views on a new procedural model, models3d/primitive-streak.js
(1,620 lines). All 8 original beat narrations carried verbatim; 13 of 15 original structure narrations
carried verbatim onto successor parts; 2 beats and 3 structure narrations are new and marked so in
narration_from. Nothing deferred: no two of the 10 rendered frames are identical.

WHAT IS SOLVED RATHER THAN TUNED. The examinable sentence is "the lower layer is not the old hypoblast
renamed", so the constraint is a conservation: every cubic micron of definitive endoderm, intraembryonic
mesoderm and notochordal process must have come through the groove or the pit. K (delivery per unit of
groove length) is solved in closed form from the MEASURED volumes of the three built layers at t=1
against the measured time-integral of the groove's own length; dEndo(t) and dMeso(t) are solved by
bisection at every t against the built-grid volumes. Worst conservation residual across 13 stages:
3.5e-9. Perturbing hVent, hMeso or wMax moves all three; perturbing the dorsal convexity moves none,
which is the declared negative control for the planar quadrature.

WHAT I PROVED (viz-training/tools/render-primitive-streak.mjs, 10 checks, proof.json committed):
 1 renders - 10 beat frames composed as the player composes them (ops, per-structure opacity, camera
   on the ISOLATE subject) + 4 full builds. 2 console clean - 0 events, 4 swiftshader driver messages
   filtered by an exact named pattern. 3 normals - face-vs-vertex winding 1.0000 over every triangle at
   7 stages x 3 variants; every signed volume positive; ray cast 0 of 10,287 first hits facing away.
   4 looks like the thing - I looked, and it found two defects no measure had (see below). 5 adapter -
   63 refs through the real viz3d.js, each at its own beat's t and flags, all with geometry, 0 failures.
   6 winding convention re-measured on a unit sphere. 7 perturbation incl. a negative control.
   8 3.z pair test, 68 construction pairs named in a published partition, worst unnamed 0.009.
   9 all 10 frames pairwise distinct. 10 every part edge-balanced (0 unbalanced half-edges).
 Model acceptance: 44 rows pass, 44 negatives all rejected. check-beat-claims: 58 claims, 0 failures,
 every beat pinned to its own instant. measure-scene-visibility: 10/10 beats, every structure a beat
 draws or points at is seeable. validate-scenes: valid, 0 warnings.

WHAT LOOKING AT THE RENDER CAUGHT THAT NOTHING ELSE DID. (a) The cells were 60 um across - wider than
the whole disc is thick - so in section they hung below the ventral lamina like beads. Now 22 um.
Every measure in the file was about where the cells are; none about how big. (b) Two holes in the disc
wherever a beat showed the epiblast without the membranes, because the membranes OWN their footprint of
both laminae. The visibility walk passed both: it checks that shown structures are visible, not that
unshown ones leave no hole.

A RENDER-KIT DEFECT, REPORTED NOT FIXED. A kit tube whose radius reaches exactly zero at one end, capped
at the other, is non-manifold at the capped rim: sweptShell writes the flat end discs through triN which
drops a degenerate triangle, so a zero-radius end gets no disc, stripFlatCap's own
`pos.count === hull + 6*ring` assertion then fails and it returns the geometry UNSTRIPPED, leaving the
flat disc coincident under the dome - the exact defect tubeCapped exists to remove, on every arrowhead
in this corpus. Section 10b of the harness reproduces it in 5 lines with a positive control. Not fixed
from a build run: render-kit is shared by every model. This model blunts its arrowheads to 6% instead.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT, all in the scene's gaps[] with numbers: the disc's growth through week 3
(held at 1.0 mm); the HANDEDNESS, which is DECLARED and not proved - the model exports axesProved:false
and beat 8's leftward sweep is pinned against the declaration, not against anything outside the file;
beat 5's framing (a median section of a 1 mm x 0.03 mm disc is a 7:1 strip - waived with the arithmetic,
and beat 3 clears the floor at 17.5% without a waiver, which is the evidence); the dysgenesis variant,
built and proved and drawn by no beat; the uncut ingression/route parts, built and named by no beat;
sub-row front non-monotonicity below t=0.15 (volumes are monotone exactly; the mesoderm there is 1e-4

Root cause: the scene had no sec_/tv_ variant of membranes, though cutx and cuty both build one -- the section structure lists were written from the LAYER list and a membrane is not a layer. FIX, scene-side only, no model change: added sec_membranes (primitive-streak#membranes+cutx) and tv_membranes (#membranes+cuty), shown in beats 3/5 and 4, plus SHOW_STRUCTURE membranes on beat 2. Framing-neutral and measured BEFORE writing: beat 5's isolate group box is x[-3.34,0.02] y[-4.93,4.93] z[-0.55,0.73] with and without the membranes, identical; beat 4's x[-2.81,2.81] y[-4.93,-1.13] z[-0.77,0.26], identical. F3 -- OPEN, AND THE ONLY THING THIS ROUND ASKS FOR. A hole in the DORSAL SURFACE of the disc on the midline immediately cranial of the node, where no dorsal part exists in the model at all -- not epiblast, streak, groove, node or pit. Fine scan at x=0, t=0.44: pit ends at y 0.96 at thickness 0.287, NOTHING from y 0.99 to 1.14, epiblast resumes at y 1.17 at its full 0.280. Both sides terminate at full thickness with 0.18 units of nothing between them, so it is not a taper. Extent: t 0.33 x[-0.48,0.48] y[-0.95,0.25] (108x125 um); t 0.44/0.52/0.58 y[-0.25,1.15] (108x145 um); t 0.70 y[-0.60,0.75]; t 0.80 shrinking to 60x15 um; absent at t 0.20, closed by t 0.86. At worst about 3% of the disc's area, and a 0.27-unit-deep notch in the dorsal surface (at y 1.05 the topmost thing in the column is mesoderm at z -0.246, where one row cranially epiblast tops out at z -0.519).

HOW I KNOW IT REACHES A STUDENT: beat 8 (t 0.46) draws epiblast, streak, groove, node, pit, laterality, membranes and NO endoderm or mesoderm, so nothing sits behind the gap -- 925 pixels of exact background colour (14,22,38) lie inside the disc outline just cranial of the node in beat08_posterior.png, a clean dark triangle cut through the epiblast. Beat 7 shows the same gap filled by mesoderm and the notochordal rod sitting a quarter-unit below the epiblast surface, on the beat that teaches a dorsal and a ventral surface.

WHY IT IS WRONG: the epiblast is a continuous epithelium over the whole disc and there is no opening in it cranial to the node at any stage. The one real opening here, the neurenteric canal, runs through the PIT, and this model correctly refuses to draw it (row I2, the pit is a dimple not a hole). So the geometry denies the opening that exists and draws one that does not, 0.2 units away.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: row P1 asserts 'on every row the named pieces cover the disc's full width with no gap left over' and passes, because P1 is a statement about each quadrature ROW across x. This gap is roughly eight consecutive rows MISSING along y. P1 proves every row is covered across its width; nothing proves consecutive rows are contiguous along the length. It is F1's shape rotated ninety degrees, in the same regionsAt() bookkeeping that gaps[] entry 26 already declares a one-row transition in -- failing by eight rows in the other axis, undeclared.

FIX: the medial lane boundaries in regionsAt() decide it. Moving them moves the epiblast's volume and therefore K, dEndo(t) and dMeso(t), so the conservation and the battery have to re-run -- which is why this was not taken scene-side here. Add the contiguity row with it: consecutive quadrature rows must be contiguous to a stated tolerance, or the gap is declared with its size.

DECLARED GAP THAT CAN BE CLOSED, NOT A DEFECT: axesProved:false is too strong and the handedness is PROVED CORRECT. viz3d VIEW_DIR.posterior=[0,0,-1] is used as camera.position=target+dir*d so the camera sits at -z; camera.up is never assigned so three.js's default (0,1,0) holds; lookAt then gives screen-right = -x. The anatomical frame is right-handed (RAS: R x A = S), and the model declares CRANIAL=+y and VENTRAL=+z, which FORCES R=-x and LEFT=+x -- those two are not free choices (the oropharyngeal membrane is cranial by definition; the epiblast faces the amniotic cavity, which is dorsal), so the third axis cannot be flipped without making the frame left-handed. The arrow is built x -1.95 to +1.95 with head=arc.slice(13), arrowhead at +x, row X reads 0.491; +x is screen-left and in a dorsal view screen-left is the embryo's left. The frame agrees. A build run should add the row and flip the flag.

THE ROUND-4 REVIEW'S OWN RESULT, in its words, for whoever picks this up (full text: ESCALATIONS.md from its heading, and the last BUILD-LOG.md entry):
 - F4, FIXED IN-ROUND, scene-side, no model change: beats 1, 7 and 10 drew the dorsal lamina with holes where the groove, node and pit own footprint the beat did not draw — beat 1 reading as a 2,229-px hole in the first picture of the topic, beat 7 (t 0.58) as a 324-column canyon down the streak on the beat that teaches a dorsal and a ventral surface, beat 10 24 columns. Beat 5 (cutx, t 0.52) 293 columns — streak 109, groove 105, node 48, pit 31 — and NO scene-side fix exists: the parts owning the dorsal lamina on the median plane are exactly the parts standing in front of the two route arrows the beat is about, and with all four shown endo_route falls 0.033 -> 0.010 and meso_route 0.027 -> 0.003, both under the floor. Dropping sec_streak gives the identical figures, so it is the groove and the pit, not the band, and no subset closes the gap and keeps the beat. Beat 5 left exactly as it was, gap open and declared in gaps[] with its figures.
 - ESCALATED under BOTH limbs of section 3. Progress: round 3 started 0 and ended 1; round 4 started 1 and ends 1 — flat twice in a row. Decision: the cause is that the model's partition gives every sub-part EXCLUSIVE, OPAQUE ownership of its footprint, so the epiblast is a sheet with the groove/node/pit shapes punched out rather than a sheet they sit in. Every beat must carry the whole plug set or draw a hole, and on beat 5 carrying the plug set and teaching the beat are mutually exclusive. F2, F4 and F5 are three instances of that one cause in two rounds. The two candidate fixes (a per-beat opacity flag for the section's dorsal parts, or making the epiblast own its full footprint and drawing sub-parts over it) are a build decision and a curriculum-cost decision, not a reviewer's call. The question is in ESCALATIONS.md as two yes/no parts.
 - STANDARDS GAP PROPOSED (section 4): every beat is checked for what it does NOT draw — for each beat, at its own t and flags, count the columns where the model has lamina geometry and the beat's shown set has none; zero, or declared with size and owner. Row P3 walks the full model, the visibility walk asks only whether shown structures are seeable, and a hole is not a structure, so neither tool has a side that can fail on this. Between them they passed a 2,229-pixel hole.

Overstated, not hidden, but a future run should not go looking for it.

STANDARDS GAP THIS TRANSCRIPTION ITSELF EXPOSES, proposed under section 4 and worth more than this repair. The read-back rule in REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT 0 says to re-read BUILD-QUEUE.json "before you set an item to done, changes-requested or escalated" — i.e. it guards the reads BEFORE the write. Nothing guards the write ITSELF, and a status write is the last thing a run does, so a run that verifies everything and then loses its final commit reports a clean escalation and leaves no trace in the queue. The rule should be: AFTER the status write, re-read the item out of the repo and confirm status, review_rounds and reviewed_at are the values you set; if they are not, re-apply before writing the log line that says you escalated. A run's log is written from intent and is therefore not evidence that the queue moved. Second occurrence in three days argues for this being a tool — queue-set.mjs could re-read and diff after releasing its lock — rather than another paragraph of prose asking runs to be careful.

findings: F1 · BEAT 5 NEVER SHOWS A CREST CELL AT THE SEAM, WHICH IS THE BEAT'S ENTIRE SUBJECT. Beat 5 is "The cells that walk away from the seam" and its narration is about the moment of fusion: "the cells at the very tips of the folds join neither the tube nor the skin". Measured on the re-rendered frame (models-out/.../beat05-superior.png): crest-coloured pixels appear in ONE panel only, the closed tube, 1,929 px; the plate, groove and folds panels have 0 between them. The folds panel IS the moment the narration describes and it shows nothing there. This is not absent geometry: vertsByKey(0.583333, {sections:true}) puts 18 crest bodies in the build, several inside the folds panel's own box (x -2.32..-2.16, z 0.60..0.75), so they are being drawn too small or occluded by the neuroepithelium at this camera. Nothing in the battery notices, because B5-only (crestCount >= 80, measured 246), B5-spread and B5-depth all measure the WHOLE build and never a panel. FIX IS AN AUTHORING DECISION, not a reviewer's guess: bigger clusters at the fold stage, a different camera for this beat, or an explicit visibility waiver saying the seam cells are sub-pixel here and why.

F2 · THE NOTOCHORD IS A THIRD OF THE DIAMETER IN ONE PANEL OF BEAT 5. After this round's fix all four panels carry a rod, but beat 5's plate panel rod measures 0.217 units across against 0.600 for the other three (built spans, vertsByKey at t=0.583333). Cause is the caudal fade in addNotochord, whose radius floors at 0.085 against R_NOTO 0.30; beat 5's plate station is v=0.1425, down near V_CAUD. The rod does taper caudally, so this may be correct anatomy rather than a defect - but on a figure sold as "four slabs of ONE build at ONE instant" beside three full-calibre rods it reads as an error, and a student drawing from it cannot tell which it is. DECIDE: either keep it and say so in sec_notochord's narration (one clause: the rod thins towards the tail), or floor the calibre inside the sections variant. The review did not choose, because changing a taper that row G and B2-contact both measure is not a change to make blind.

F3 · BEAT 4'S NARRATION INSTRUCTS SOMETHING THE FRAME CANNOT DO. It says "Compare the two sections side by side, because the mechanism predicts the lesion" and the frame is a single longitudinal view of the tail - there are no two sections in it. gaps[] already records that the median-section variant is not built, which explains the absence but does not reconcile the sentence with the picture; a student told to compare two sections and shown one will assume they have missed something. Either build the median-section variant (gaps[] calls it the proper fix for beats 4 and 9 both) or amend that one sentence. Amending narration carried across VERBATIM is a content call and the review did not make it.

F4 · ACCEPTANCE ROW Q IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE, AND THAT UNDERMINES EVERY "ALL ROWS PASS" IN THIS ITEM'S HISTORY. Seven identical runs of the harness against the same file in one sitting: six passed row Q, one failed it. Failing pairs, both NORMAL variant at day 25: lateral_mesoderm|notochord frac 0.05940 and lateral_mesoderm|somites frac 0.07076, against OVERLAP_MAX 0.005. This round's change touches only the sections variant and cannot reach them - the same code passed the row once immediately before and four times immediately after. Full failing log committed at viz-training/models-out/neurulation-neural-plate-tube/_rowQ-flake-2026-10-03.txt. LIKELY MECHANISM, NOT PROVED: both pairs are tissues that abut, and insideFrac decides containment by casting a ray along +x from each sampled vertex and counting parity, which is a knife-edge for a vertex lying ON a shared surface. The review states only what it measured: the row is not reproducible. This is not local to this item - insideFrac and row Q are shared, so "23 acceptance rows pass" is an unstable sentence wherever it appears. Candidate fixes for whoever takes it: add the two abutting pairs to TOUCH_OK with a measured justification, or offset the ray origin off-surface along the vertex normal before the parity test.

F5 · TWO INSTRUMENTS WERE NOT RE-RUN AFTER THIS ROUND'S CHANGE, AND THE ITEM MUST NOT GO done UNTIL THEY ARE. The sections variant now cuts at different stations, so the numbers in _visibility-walk.txt and _fragments.txt for beats 1, 2 and 5 are stale. tools/measure-scene-visibility.mjs would not boot in the review container - page.waitForFunction timed out on window.__ready after 30s with an empty console log, so the walk page is missing an asset that container did not have. tools/measure-fragments.mjs was not attempted. What WAS re-run, in the review's own container, against the committed file: the 12-check render harness (ALL CHECKS PASS), 24 acceptance rows, 24 negative cases, the 3 perturbations, and all 36 beat claims re-measured through claimMeasure at each beat's own t.

F6 · CROSS-TASK CONTRACT BUG, FOUND BY BEING ITS VICTIM MID-RUN. This review claimed the item in-review at 05:37:09Z. At 06:09:23Z the BUILD run reclaimed it to built, calling it a dead claim "stale_for_hours: 4.7" - 32 minutes into a live review. Cause: queue-set.mjs --status in-review updates status and updated_at but does NOT refresh claimed_at, and the build task measures staleness from claimed_at, which still held the BUILD run's own 01:26:24Z. REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT section 1 correctly measures staleness from updated_at; BUILD-TASK-PROMPT does not. So EVERY review of an item whose build claim is more than two hours old is declared dead almost immediately, and the two tasks can be on one item at once - exactly what section 5 forbids. Nothing was lost this time, only because the build run left findings and review_rounds untouched and built nothing. It will not always be harmless. FIX: make the build task's staleness read updated_at, or make queue-set.mjs refresh claimed_at on every status change. This round set claimed_at itself as a stopgap. This is a decision about the two task prompts, which neither task may edit, so it needs Frank.

F7 · A GAP IN THE STANDARD, not in this model (REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT section 4). The defect this round fixed - three notochords under four panels - passed every existing check, and it passed them for a structural reason that will let the next one through too. The mechanical review asks that every scene key resolve to something the model builds and that every built key appear in the scene or in gaps[]: both held, because resolution is per-MODEL. The visibility walk asks that each structure be visible in a beat's frame: that holds too, because it is per-BEAT - three rods out of four is plenty of ink. Nothing anywhere asks a question per PANEL. So in any multi-panel variant (sections, sbPanel) a structure can be built, resolvable, and visibly present in the frame as a whole while being absent from one panel, and no instrument looks. PROPOSED RULE for ARTWORK-STANDARD section 3: where a variant lays out N panels of one geometry, every structure the beat shows must be counted PER PANEL, and a structure legitimately absent from one panel must declare it. New acceptance row X is that rule applied to one structure in one model; it belongs in the standard, not only here.

R2 STANDARDS GAP (REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT section 4). Nothing in either standard requires that two structures a beat asks the student to tell apart be distinguishable. ARTWORK-STANDARD section 3 checks key resolution, containment, coincidence, contact, arrowheads and per-panel ink. RENDER-STANDARD's only colour rule is 2.2, which governs sRGB-vs-linear ENCODING — that a colour arrives undistorted, not that it differs from the colour beside it. measure-scene-visibility.mjs measures INK as a fraction of frame and WOULD PASS A FRAME IN WHICH EVERY STRUCTURE WAS THE IDENTICAL COLOUR. That is why this reached built twice with every gate green. Proposed rule drafted in the escalation entry: where a beat's narration asks the student to tell two structures apart, or where two structures lie across a boundary the scene exists to teach (maternal/fetal, arterial/venous, parent/derivative), their declared colours must differ by at least dE76 20; same tissue at two stages may share a hue and must differ by at least dE76 10. findings: 1 · ANATOMICAL, MARKABLE. Heuser's membrane is drawn as the SECONDARY yolk sac's own wall. models3d/bilaminar-embryonic-disc.js:629-643 builds the single mesh keyed 'heuser' (label 'Exocoelomic (Heuser's) membrane') around whichever sac is alive: rY = max(primLive ? primR : 0, secLive ? secR : 0). Once primary_gone (WHEN=0.95) the primary is dead and secLive=1, so at t=1 the membrane is rebuilt at rY=secR. MEASURED at t=1: heuser maxR_xz 1.155 wrapping secondary_yolk_sac 1.150, identical y-range [-1.28,-0.10]. Beat 10 SHOWs it at day 14. This is wrong: Heuser's (exocoelomic) membrane lines the PRIMARY yolk sac / exocoelomic cavity; the secondary yolk sac is lined by a second wave of hypoblast-derived extraembryonic endoderm, and what is left of the primary and its membrane is pinched off as the exocoelomic cysts. The model contradicts itself on this: line 906 says 'the membrane is the secondary sac's own wall' while line 923 says a cyst 'may still lie against its old wall'. A student would be marked wrong on what lines the definitive yolk sac. FIX: gate the heuser mesh on D.primLive alone and let secondary_yolk_sac carry its own surface — which also fixes finding 3 for that sac.

2 · THE ACCEPTANCE BATTERY IS BEING SILENCED BY THE SAME ERROR. CONTACT_PARTITION (models3d/bilaminar-embryonic-disc.js:896) is the published dictionary of overlapping pairs 'excluded as construction rather than anatomy', and it is what acceptance row P (P_no_unexcused_shared_space) consults. Its entry 'heuser|secondary_yolk_sac': 'the membrane is the secondary sac's own wall' excuses precisely the overlap finding 1 is about. Row P therefore reports 0 and CANNOT fail on it. The row built to catch two structures occupying one space is being quieted by an anatomically false excuse. When finding 1 is fixed, that entry must be DELETED rather than reworded, and row P re-run to confirm it still reads 0 for the right reason.

3 · EVERY LUMEN IS HIDDEN UNDER ITS OWN WALL, SO THREE BEATS HIGHLIGHT SOMETHING INVISIBLE. The cavity meshes are enclosed by near-coincident shell meshes (amnion sits 0.009 outside amniotic_cavity radially and 0.040 taller; heuser sits 0.005 outside secondary_yolk_sac). MEASURED by me, beat 10's own structure set at t=1, lateral camera: hiding amniotic_cavity altogether changes 7 pixels (0.003% of subject); applying beat 10's own HIGHLIGHT_STRUCTURE amniotic_cavity intensity 0.85 changes 45 pixels (0.021%). A student clicking or watching that highlight sees nothing happen. measure-scene-visibility's id-pick pass agrees — beat 10 id-pick: amnion 11.679, heuser 10.934, amniotic_cavity 0.036, secondary_yolk_sac 0.301 — and the builder's own render harness printed 'pixels amniotic_cavity, day 14 visible=0' in the run that marked the item built. Also affects beat 6 (secondary_yolk_sac id-pick 0) and beat 7 (amniotic_cavity 0.002, connecting_stalk 0.018). FIX is a design call for the build run: either highlight the wall, or give the wall a cutaway, or drop the redundant lumen mesh where the wall already reads as the cavity. NOT a curriculum question, so not escalated.

4 · STANDARDS GAP (RENDER-STANDARD / measure-scene-visibility). measure-scene-visibility passes beat 10 by crediting amniotic_cavity as 'seen through translucent material' (alpha-aware 11.065%, peak 140) when its id-pick share is 0.036%. 'Some of this structure's colour reaches the camera' is the wrong question for a beat that HIGHLIGHTS the structure; the right question is 'does toggling or highlighting it change the picture'. PROPOSED RULE: where a beat points at a structure with HIGHLIGHT_STRUCTURE or TRACE_STRUCTURE, the walk must also measure the highlight delta — render the beat with and with the highlight applied and require a floor on changed pixels — and must not pass that structure on alpha-aware credit alone. Had that rule existed, this scene would not have reached review with three such beats.

ROUND 2 · BLOCKING, ESCALATED (reason 3). primary_yolk_sac, heuser and extraembryonic_mesoderm are NEVER DRAWN IN THE PLAYER, in any beat, at any t. Measured two ways: walk-scene-in-player visible counts 4/6, 4/6, 1/4, 4/6, 3/4 on beats 1, 3, 4, 5, 7; and a direct probe of the live player's mesh table lists 13 keys with those three absent. MECHANISM, in viz3d.js and deliberate: the mesh table is built once at the adapter default t=1, and restage() filters meshStructs on 'meshes[s.key] &&' so only structures that ALREADY have a mesh are rebuilt at a new t. All three end before day 14, so they never get a first mesh and SET_STAGE can never give them one. COST: beat 1 promises 'a balloon above it and a balloon below' and shows nothing below; beat 3 'A cavity on each side' shows one; beat 4 exists only to show extraembryonic mesoderm as one tissue, HIGHLIGHTs it at 0.9, and renders a featureless grey ball (cytotrophoblast 100% of subject, nothing else visible); beat 5's splanchnic sheet covers a yolk sac that is not there; beat 7 teaches the secondary sac is SMALLER than the primary with no primary on screen. Claims B1-below, B3-primary and B6-both all PASS because they ask the model whether the mesh exists, not whether the picture shows it. NOT SENT BACK because the three fixes are three decisions: change restage() in the shared player for 146 scenes; or keep the transient structures alive at t=1, which contradicts row R and claim B10-primary-gone; or declare each stage as its own pinned-ref structure, which undoes the design decision SET_STAGE embodies. Round 1's anatomically CORRECT Heuser fix is what made it undrawable - before it, heuser existed at t=1 and the player held a mesh. Full account and the decision needed: ESCALATIONS.md 2026-10-03 11:55Z. 19 of 146 scenes use SET_STAGE at t<1 and 15 of those are already escalated; correlation only, not verified.

findings: ROUND 1, 2026-10-03. Mechanical review PASSES in full: builds at every required t, console clean, winding 1.000000 and 0 unpaired edges over 722,528 triangles, ray cast 0/6512, 72+36 adapter refs resolved, 51 beat claims hold with every beat pinned, validate-scenes 146/146 in-repo, and NO view repeats the one before it (measured on the player frames: every consecutive pair moves 30.7-58.9% of pixels by >40/255). Dorsoventral polarity verified independently at t=0.05/0.17/0.24/0.93: amniotic cavity y>0, both yolk sacs y<0, epiblast above hypoblast at every stage. THREE OPEN FINDINGS. (1) BEAT 10 AND BEAT 5: amniotic_cavity clears the 40/255 visibility floor by ONE UNIT - peak 41 on beat 10 and 44 on beat 5, measured on a CORRECTED player frame (see the log). Cause is the palette, not the geometry: amn_cav #5dade2 and amnion #85c1e9 differ by at most 40/255 in any channel before lighting and opacity, so removing the cavity leaves almost the same colour behind. Rebuilt at PH_N/TH_N 36x72 - an anatomically neutral change - beat 10 drops to peak 33 and the walk FAILS with NOT SEEABLE ON EITHER MEASURE. This is the same defect the build run diagnosed and fixed BY RECOLOURING on the immediately preceding item (bilaminar-embryonic-disc, same morning: taking it away left almost the same colour behind); the palette comment says these blues were carried over from the SVG era and the known hazard was not re-checked against them. The fix is a colour, not an opacity - the log already records that dropping the cavity opacity to 0.18 traded one failure for three. (2) BEAT 10, RENDER-STANDARD 3.ab: chorionic_cavity, the beat OWN highlighted subject at intensity 0.95, draws in 34 connected components after the sub-4px hairline discount (293 raw) with the largest holding only 57.3% of its ink, total ink 2.06% of frame - player frame, 40/255. UNCHANGED by the depthWrite fix, so this one is real and not an artefact. The chorionic cavity is a single continuous space and the beat exists to show it closing; a student sees a broken ring of patches. (3) BEAT 5 NARRATES A FIVE-WEEK SCAN AT DAY 16, WHERE THIS MODEL OWN SAC IS 1.5 mm. The narration is explicitly sonographic - the gestational sac on a five-week scan is the chorionic cavity, the double bleb, the finding that says the pregnancy is genuinely in the uterus. Five weeks MENSTRUAL is day 21 post-fertilisation and a real five-week gestational sac is about 5 mm mean diameter. The beat sits at day 16 (= 4w2d menstrual) with chorSacDiamMm 1.516, while day 21 - which this model ALREADY builds, at exactly 5.0 mm, as beat 6 B6-pin asserts - is the day the sentence describes. The day claim was written as the beat sits in week three rather than against the five weeks the narration actually says, so nothing could catch it. The file own header says getting this two-week offset wrong is the single easiest way to be wrong by a lot in this topic; the conversion was done scrupulously for the three fit inputs and not for this beat anchor. Same family, lower stakes: beat 3 B3-size calls 268 um the few hundred microns an early scan sees, where a sonographic yolk sac is 3-5 mm. FIXED BY THIS REVIEW, in the tooling and not in the item: measure-scene-visibility.mjs set transparent and opacity on every structure and never depthWrite, leaving three default true, where viz3d sets depthWrite = op >= 0.98 in two places. Every DoubleSide translucent shell was occluding ITSELF in a sawtooth of wedges along its limb, in every beat, corpus-wide. It survived finer tessellation, silhouettes off, a 1000x near-plane sweep and the removal of every other structure before the one-line fix removed it completely. It had already manufactured a false 3.ab defect on this item: beat 8 connecting_stalk read as 2 components with the largest holding 84.5%, and reads 1 component at 99.4% once the tool draws what the player draws. NOT a defect in this model.

ROUND 2, 2026-10-03, by a run that did not build it. CORRECTED IN THIS REVIEW: the definitive yolk sac was not attached to the hypoblast in beats 4, 5 and 6. models3d/amniotic-cavity-yolk-sac.js had two declared laws that disagreed about when the vitelline duct exists - rVitelline() declares it born over days VD_OPEN(22) to 26, while vdLength()'s first term 0.25*Rys(day) carried NO ramp, so the sac was hung a duct-length below the hypoblast on every day from day 8 with nothing drawn in the gap. Measured on built vertices within r=2 of the axis: at day 13 hypoblast ventral y -2.8436 against secondary yolk sac dome y -7.5071, a 4.664-unit void, 82% of the whole disc's thickness, about 41 um at the beat's own scale; at day 21, 4.470. Beat 4 shows hypoblast_cut and secondary_yolk_sac_cut with no primary_yolk_sac and no exocoelomic_membrane, so the frame draws the definitive yolk sac as a ball floating free under the disc - in the three beats whose narration teaches 'hypoblast for the yolk sac' and 'the definitive yolk sac hanging below it'. FIX: the first term now carries rVitelline's OWN birth ramp, rampDay(day, VD_OPEN, 26) - the model made consistent with itself, not a new constant. rampDay=1 from day 26, so every day from 26 on is unchanged BY CONSTRUCTION and beats 7-11 are bit-identical. Day 13 now separates by gapAt(rys)=0.398, the inset every adjacent pair in the file carries. RE-PROVED AFTER THE CHANGE: harness ALL CHECKS PASS (0 unpaired edges over 722,528 tris, face-vs-vertex 1.000000000000, ray cast 0 of 6512, battery all rows with 23 negatives rejected, 25/25 verbatim, clock 1e-9); walk 11/11; check-beat-claims 51 claims 0 failures 0 unpinned; validate-scenes 146/146 in-repo. Scene provenance carries corrected_at/corrected_by/correction_note. THREE LEFT OPEN. (1) DAY-21 SEPARATION ONLY HALVED, 2.78 units remain, and the cause is a DIFFERENT clamp: yOutside binds, amnVentral = yAmn + (A.b+thAm)*cos(amnPhMax) puts the amnion's drawn ventral edge at y -18.3 true-scale while the disc half-thickness is about 1.3, so the sac is pushed below an amnion that has already wrapped 18 units past the disc on day 21. At day 21 the amnion is still a dorsal dome attached at the epiblast rim and does not descend ventrally until folding. THE QUESTION IS amnPhMax's GROWTH LAW, NOT THE CLAMP - the clamp is correct and its comment says why. Not touched: it feeds row E-shell and the coelom computation and deserves its own measurement. (2) BEAT 9 DRAWS NEITHER DESTINATION ITS NARRATION NAMES. 'The vitelline duct runs to the ileum ... The allantois runs to the bladder.' The beat shows only hypoblast, vitelline_duct_closing, allantois, secondary_yolk_sac. The allantois ends bluntly in open space. primitive_gut IS built at that t (y -6.77..3.16) but is not shown, and showing it would not help because it sits inside an opaque hypoblast dome. gaps[] declares no bladder; it does NOT declare an allantois terminating in nothing. (3) THE COMB ON BEAT 10's LIMB - A MEASURED SIXTH ELIMINATION, AND IT RULES OUT DEPTH. Rendering amnion ALONE at t=0.93: as-is PRESENT; opaque GONE; side FrontSide GONE; outer surface only GONE; inner surface only PRESENT; depthTest false PRESENT. So it is transparent DOUBLE-SIDED blending of the shell's own inner surface, and it is NOT a depth-buffer effect - turning the depth test off does not touch it. One mesh alone in an empty scene, so no neighbour can be implicated. Proposed RENDER-STANDARD section 4 rung, above the depth rung: a comb of translucent wedges along a shell's limb is double-sided blend order until proved otherwise; render the part alone, opaque, and with FrontSide, and if either removes it stop. FrontSide is safe for a watertight correctly-wound shell in any non-section view. NOT applied: side is set centrally in render-kit/viz3d and every _cut/_cutz beat needs DoubleSide, so it is a kit-level change needing all 146 scenes re-proved. NOT DEFECTS, recorded so round 3 does not re-raise them: the hollow inside the bilaminar disc is deliberate and documented at buildDisc (two shells of one ellipsoid meeting at the equator with EQ_PAD, hollow so no third layer pre-empts trilaminar-disc); the exocoelomic cyst apparently inside the yolk sac in beat 4 is PROJECTION not intersection (cysts sit on a shell of radius (rExmIn-gapAt)*0.70 ~35 outside a sac of radius 17 at y~-20, and PARTITION is right to have no such pair); a 404 seen in a staged-subset harness run is /config.js, a staging gap, not the model.
