findings: F1 · BEAT 4 DRAWS NOTHING MEETING ANYTHING. The beat is titled 'The first pouch meets the first cleft' and narrates 'a three-layered sheet stands between them'. At beat 4's own t (0.647059, day 44) the three solids never touch: pouch1 to tympanic_membrane 13.23 units = 0.613 of an intersegment; tympanic_membrane to cleft1 17.82 = 0.826 seg; pouch1 to cleft1 41.66 = 1.932 seg. The membrane's own bbox diagonal there is 31.06, so the two voids are 43 and 57 percent of the membrane itself. The gap is not a stage: pouch1-to-cleft1 is 1.932 seg at EVERY t from 0.35 to 0.94 - the three are placed at fixed fractional radii and never approach. HOW I KNOW: nearest-vertex distance between the right-side solids of each pair, model built through the real three.js, printed at six t. VISIBLE: render beat 4 from 'anterior' and you see six objects in three widely separated pairs with empty space between. It is invisible from 'lateral', the camera the beat stands at, because lateral looks straight down the axis the gap lies on. A student is being taught that the first pharyngeal membrane is where endoderm and ectoderm are in direct apposition; this picture teaches that there is a wide tissue space on both sides of it.

F2 · BEAT 4'S TWO APPOSITION CLAIMS CANNOT DETECT F1, AND NEITHER CAN BEAT 5'S TRAIL CLAIM. B4-apart's text is 'the pouch and the cleft do NOT run into one another - endoderm and ectoderm stay separate, with the membrane between' and its measure is relSize.tympanic_membrane atLeast 0.8 - the membrane's own extent. B4-membrane's measure is screenHeightOverSeg.tympanic_membrane.lateral, a screen height on the single camera that projects the gap to zero. B5-trail's text is 'the strand has been drawn out a long way behind the descending thymus, and every ectopic site lies on it' and its measure is relSize.thymopharyngeal_duct atLeast 1.2 - again the thing's own size. Three claims about where structures are RELATIVE TO EACH OTHER, all measured as the size of one of them. They cannot fail for the reason their text states. The fix is a measure of the shape 'minimum distance between key A and key B over the mean of their own extents', asserted at the beat's own t.

Among the eight structures beat 1 shows together, the next-closest pair after that blue cluster is dE 23.2 - so cleft1, clefts_lower and pouch4 form one tight blue group with clear air to everything else in the frame. It is a corpus convention, not a local one: ectoderm is blue in notochord.js (0x2980b9), trilaminar-disc (0x2980b9), neurulation (0x2980b9), body-cavity-coelom and lateral-folding (0x2f7fc4), and the sibling pharyngeal-arches.js (0x85c1e9, 0x9fb4c9). F1 [MECHANICAL - BLOCKING. The recorded proof is stale.] The harness viz-training/tools/render-pharyngeal-clefts-membranes.mjs now ends in PROOF FAILED on check 11. F2 [ANATOMICAL - same root cause as F1.] The model builds NO BODY SURFACE, so the four clefts are grooves in nothing. The model's complete set of addAll keys is arch_bars, auricular_hillocks, branchial_cyst, branchial_fistula, branchial_sinus_tract, carotid_external, carotid_internal, cervical_sinus, cleft, epipericardial_ridge, meatal_plug, meatus_lumen, membranes_lower, operculum, pouch - there is no surface ectoderm among them. With F_CLEFT = 3.60 the four crescents sit 3.6 intersegments out from a pharyngeal half-width of 0.80 with nothing drawn in between. SEE THE PICTURE, which is where this was found: viz-training/models-out/pharyngeal-clefts-membranes/d44-superior.png shows the pharynx and both carotids as a small cluster at the centre of the frame and the clefts, operculum and cervical sinus as arcs out at the rim, with empty space across the whole middle; d34-lateral.png shows the four crescents hanging unattached. Beat 1's narration says "On the outside, surface ectoderm dips between them as four pairs of grooves" and beat 6 says the sinus is "sealed off from the surface": the student is told about a surface the model never draws. This is the SAME defect, in the same words, that the pouches review wrote up and repaired - "four crescents attached to nothing, under a narration that calls a cleft 'a groove on the OUTSIDE', which is a feature of a surface". The builder flagged the proportion honestly as the weakest part of the item and was right; what their note did not say is that no surface exists at all. F1 and F2 are ONE repair: port the sibling's solved surface.

F3 [ANATOMICAL, AND THE PROOF DOES NOT TEST ITS CLAIM.] The carotid relation is never shown, and the check that says it is passes on an axis that cannot see it. (a) Beat 11 is the ONLY beat that draws carotid_internal and carotid_external, and its narration says of the cyst: "its tract runs between the internal and external carotid arteries - which is why treatment is complete excision rather than drainage." Measured at that beat's own t=0.941176: branchial_cyst is 3.08 intersegments from carotid_internal and 3.10 from carotid_external, lateral to both. From beat 11's lateral camera the cyst projects neatly between the two vessels and looks right; this was found by rotating, which is why section 2 asks for it. (b) The claim that IS measured, B12-between, belongs to beat 12 - which draws no carotids. So the only beat whose geometry is tested for this relation never shows the vessels, and the only beat that shows the vessels is never tested. (c) The measure itself is one-axis. claimMeasure 'fistulaBetween' at models3d/pharyngeal-clefts-membranes.js:2012-2025 takes the fistula's vertices in a y-slab at the vessels' crossing level, averages their Z, and scores how far that mean z sits between ci.z and ce.z. It never reads x. Measured: 0 of 5544 branchial_fistula vertices lie inside the carotids' own x band at either t - band 37.64..55.69 at t=0.941 against a fistula minimum x of 69.01, and band 44.00..65.10 at t=1 against a minimum x of 80.67. The tract is entirely lateral of both vessels and the measure still returns 0.3941 against a bar of 0.35. Between two things on one axis is not between two things. REPAIR: the vessels must run deep to the tract's medial portion, or the tract must dive medially between them to reach the tonsillar fossa - which it already reaches, fistula-to-pouch2 is 0.01 intersegments - and fistulaBetween must require tract vertices INSIDE the carotids' x band before it scores the z bracket. NOT CORRECTED HERE: (a) and (b) move with the same lateral layout as F1, and tightening the measure on its own would turn a false pass into a failure without repairing the thing it tests.

STANDARDS GAP (section 4) - two rules proposed, neither written into the standards by this run. (1) A model that copies a constant from another model takes a DEPENDENCY on that file, and nothing in this loop re-runs a built item's harness when a model it depends on changes. This item sat `built` for fourteen hours carrying a stale copy while its own recorded proof said it passed, and only re-running the harness caught it. Propose for RENDER-STANDARD: when a model declares a copied constant, its harness must assert the copy against the SOURCE FILE's current value - a textual check that fails the moment the sibling changes - rather than against built geometry, which fails only once somebody happens to re-run it. (2) A measure whose name asserts a spatial relation must be rejected by a negative case placed outside that relation ON AN AXIS THE MEASURE DOES NOT READ. This item's acceptance battery has 21 negative cases and not one of them moves the tract laterally, which is why a z-only containment test shipped as a containment test.

items.note: AN UNPINNED PROCEDURAL REF RESOLVES AT t=1 AT MOUNT, AND A STRUCTURE THAT RESOLVES TO `none` IS NEVER RETRIED. Filed 2026-10-03 by the model3d REVIEW task from embryology__week-3-gastrulation__notochord, which it escalated for this reason. MECHANISM, read off viz3d.js: parseProceduralRef (:480) defaults an unpinned ref to t=1; mountScene builds every structure at that t; a model whose structure is TRANSIENT (exists at one stage and not another) therefore returns mergeByKey null -> reason:none -> no mesh; and restage() (:1854) filters `meshes[s.key] && adapter.stageable(s)` — its own comment says `Only structures that ARRIVED are restaged` — so SET_STAGE can never bring it back at any later t. EFFECT ON THE NOTOCHORD SCENE, measured by driving mountScene and clicking the chips: 8 of 42 structures never load; the player tells the student `Loaded 34 of 42 parts — 8 have no 3D model yet`; the greyed-out buttons include `Stage 1 — the notochordal process`, `Stage 2 — the notochordal canal` and `Stage 3 — the floor breaks down and the plate intercalates`, i.e. three of the four stages the scene teaches, each captioned `no 3D model of this structure yet` — which viz3d defines as a fact about the corpus, and is false: the model builds all three. INVISIBLE TO EVERY EXISTING CHECK because measure-scene-visibility.mjs reimplements the ops and builds the model itself (it passes that scene 11/11 and reports plate_sec at 5.271%, a structure the player does not possess), while the adapter-resolution check calls load() with each beat`s own t, which is the one path that works. RENDER-STANDARD 3.x already rules `if the two ever disagree, viz3d is right` — nothing compares them. TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, and this is the decision: (a) resolve an unpinned ref at the scene`s first/declared SET_STAGE t rather than 1, or retry `none` structures on restage — fixes every scene with transient structures at once, no scene edits; (b) make scenes pin transient refs (notochord#plate@0.4+block) — works, but tPinned refs are not stageable so those structures freeze while the rest walks the stages, and every future scene carries the workaround. The review recommends (a). SEE ESCALATIONS.md 2026-10-03 01:51Z for the full account and the two questions for Frank. DO NOT let a build run edit viz3d.js unreviewed — it serves all 146 scenes.

items.note: RULED BY FRANK 2026-09-29 via the decision desk. ISOLATE_REGION ghosts the very subject it isolates, because it never adds its keys to state.hi — the exact test paint() uses to hold a structure at its authored opacity. COMPARE_STRUCTURES two lines below already does it. Fix: state.only.forEach(k => state.hi[k] = 0.5). LAND IT IN THE SAME SITTING AS engine__refit-camera-on-isolate so viz3d.js is opened once, and IDENTIFY WHAT REVERTED THAT FILE before either change goes in. Verify through paint(), not through a direct model render — a build harness renders every layer at full opacity, which is why no proof frame has ever shown this.

VIZ3D DEFECT. Filed 2026-10-02T20:45Z by the model3d REVIEW task from round 4 of embryology__week-3-gastrulation__trilaminar-disc-3-germ-layers, which cannot fix it (viz3d.js is shared by 146 scenes) and cannot close while it stands. SYMPTOM: every beat carrying a SHOW_RELATIONSHIP op draws its connector line in the WRONG FRAME, at the wrong scale and off-centre, so it overshoots the structures it joins and runs off the viewport. MEASURED on that scene's beat 7 in the real player (walk-scene-in-player.mjs): exactly 4 subject pixels on the frame border, 2 on the top row and 2 on the bottom, all at x=383-384 of 768 (the exact midline), all colour (97,94,112) - the line's own colour, not the disc. The walk reports the beat CLIPPED and SUPPRESSES all five structure shares for it, so the clip also costs the beat its measurement. CAUSE, read in the source and confirmed independently of the build run that first reported it: viz3d.js:1424-1425 creates `holder` and `overlay` as SIBLINGS under sceneObj. The per-view refit at viz3d.js:1686-1688 re-centres and rescales ONLY holder - `holder.children.forEach(m => m.position.sub(c))` then `holder.scale.setScalar(4.2/mx)`. drawPairs() at viz3d.js:2262 takes its endpoints from center(meshes[...]), i.e. coordinates that are already holder-local, and adds the resulting THREE.Line to `overlay`, which carries an identity transform and never receives either the recentring or the 4.2/mx scale. So the line is drawn at holder-LOCAL coordinates unscaled: whenever 4.2/mx < 1 the line is drawn LONGER than the gap between the drawn meshes, which is exactly the overshoot seen. This is a sharper account than the originating run's, which recorded 'ASSUMED NOT PROVED: that the endpoints are stale by one fit' - the endpoints are not stale, the group they are added to is simply never transformed. FIX, one of: parent overlay to holder so it inherits the transform; or apply holder's matrix to the line's points when building the geometry. BLAST RADIUS UNMEASURED and that is the real work here: every scene using SHOW_RELATIONSHIP is affected, the defect is invisible unless the line happens to leave the frame, and parenting overlay to holder changes line geometry corpus-wide. A run taking this should measure how many of the 146 scenes carry SHOW_RELATIONSHIP before changing anything. RELATED: engine__refit-camera-on-isolate and engine__camera-scale-group, both escalated, are the same family - viz3d's framing and the things it forgets to frame.

items.why: Frank's call, 2026-09-10: histology moves from the unbuilt SVG/microscopy path onto procedural 3D. The honest version of this is NOT a flat picture of a slide. Build a block of tissue whose CUT FACE reads like a section, and which can be rotated. That earns its place because it settles the single most-examined point in the topic: pseudostratified epithelium LOOKS stratified in section, and rotating the block shows every cell still touching the basement membrane. A micrograph cannot show that. Also flip the four histology structures' preferred_modes to model3d and lift the course suspension in CURRICULUM.json, but ONLY once this renderer actually renders.

items.why: Procedural models are in their own units; BodyParts3D meshes are anatomical millimetres. A scene mixing both providers renders one of them as a speck. NOT urgent — every scene queued here is wholly procedural, including the four cerebellum/brainstem ones, which carry zero mesh refs. It becomes blocking the first time a scene wants procedural detail INSIDE a scanned mesh — a circle of Willis inside a brain. Fix by declaring a model's real-world extent in its module (say, the mm the model's unit box spans) and scaling in the adapter, so scenes and scene authors never see units at all.
items.blocks: any future scene that mixes procedural geometry with a BodyParts3D mesh

items.why: MEASURED IN THE LIVE APP 2026-09-10 while verifying the colour fix on a real 20-part scene. BONE_CEILING (0.78) is applied in the bodyparts3d LOAD path, but applyStyles() later does m.material.color.copy(srgbColor(s.color, ...)) on every structure, which OVERWRITES the clamped colour with the raw authored one. Proof: l2 is authored #f0dfa8, whose brightest channel is 0.94 and should clamp to 0.78 — it renders as exactly #f0dfa8. So the ceiling has never reached a student's screen.
items.note: PRE-EXISTING, NOT A REGRESSION — the same overwrite happened before the colour-space fix, so this is not something the fix introduced and it does NOT block deploying. Deliberately not changed before a deploy: fixing it would darken every bone in all 71 ready scenes, and that is a change to verify on its own, not to smuggle in alongside another one. Decide first whether the ceiling is still wanted at all: it was introduced to stop near-white bone clipping under the lights, and correct colour handling already makes bone darker than it was, so the problem it guarded against may simply be gone.

RULED BY FRANK 2026-09-29 via the decision desk. Split out of septation-of-heart. Build the conotruncal wedging the septation scene is missing: the conus shortening and rotating, and the aortic root migrating LEFT and POSTERIOR to sit over the left ventricle, then rebuild the aortic and pulmonary channels on top of that. Measured problem it exists to fix: at day 56 both great vessels arise from the right ventricle — aortic channel 0.006 from the bulbus and 0.438 from the future LV; pulmonary 0.007 and 0.538. Round 2 of septation searched 224 combinations of terminus height, position, offset and bow and found nothing better than 4 of 25 samples inside the lumen, so this is missing anatomy and not a tuning problem. Views 6, 8, 9 and 10 of the septation scene are held until this lands.

RULED BY FRANK 2026-09-29 via the decision desk. Add "primary" as an explicit third role in model3d-scene-spec-v2.md. 92 structures already use it and viz3d.js already honours it through isTaught(); the spec is what is behind. Update the schema and validate-scenes.mjs so primary is supported rather than leaving a large corpus off-spec. Do NOT rewrite the 92 structures. This has been passed down three times by build runs that were not allowed to choose.

RULED BY FRANK 2026-09-29 via the decision desk. The model owns presentation: where a scene is silent on colour or opacity, the adapter falls back to the MODEL's material instead of an opaque default, and a scene overrides only deliberately. Also do both safeguards: (1) validate-scenes.mjs ERRORS when a structure's colour differs from its model's LAYERS colour for the same key; (2) document opacity in model3d-scene-spec-v2.md including the 0.98 depthWrite threshold. Found on the coronary scene, where the model had moved three myocardial territories to amber/violet/green precisely because three reds were unreadable, and the scene still carried the old reds hex-for-hex identical to the three arteries.

RULED BY FRANK 2026-09-29 via the decision desk. T-invariant procedural models are ALLOWED. T_MEANING becomes load-bearing: a model declares that its geometry does not vary meaningfully with t, the mechanical checks recognise that declaration instead of treating trivially-true build-at-every-t checks as passes, and THE PLAYER HIDES THE TIMELINE for such a scene rather than offering a student a control that does nothing. heart-external and coronary-arteries-cardiac-veins both already declare it. Timeline stays for models where t is a real progression.

RULED BY FRANK 2026-09-29 via the decision desk. render:"anchor" must stop drawing an opaque depth-test-off sphere when the anchored thing is a WHOLE BONE rather than a point landmark — a whole bone should not be obscured by its own marker. Preserve the sphere for genuine point landmarks. Affects every anchored structure in the corpus, not just the coccyx that surfaced it.

items.why: MEASURED 2026-10-02 by the round-5 build run on embryology__gametogenesis-fertilization__blastocyst, in its own container, with a new instrument added to viz-training/tools/measure-scene-visibility.mjs in the same run. viz3d.js frameView() calls subjectBox() then distanceForBox() on EVERY view, with no memory of the previous beat, so the camera is refitted per beat and every beat is normalised to the same fill. For a PARAMETRIC PROCESS SCENE whose subject IS growth, that guarantees the quantity the model solves for can never appear on screen. On blastocyst: box_fill_pct is 75.40 on ALL TEN beats while the subject's own world box runs 15.685 -> 25.858 units and world_per_px runs 0.0215 -> 0.039526. Beat 1 (morula in its zona) and beat 8 (bare blastocyst, narrating 'half again the width of the morula') render at 33.37% and 33.33% of the frame - the same width to within 0.1% - while the model's embryoDRel at beat 8's t is 1.59. The scene was told to teach 'date days five to six correctly' and the walk shows the wall thinning and the cavity filling and never shows the embryo getting bigger.
items.found_by: the round-4 review of blastocyst (F5), which proposed the capability; the round-5 build run then measured where it belongs and filed it here rather than improvising it mid-scene, on that review round's own written instruction: "if it turns out that the scale group belongs in viz3d rather than in this scene, that is the moment to escalate it as an ENGINE item in its own right rather than cycling this scene through further rounds waiting on it."
items.escalation_reason: reason 3 - a decision no task is allowed to make, on two independent limbs. (a) THE DESIGN IS NOT THE ONE PROPOSED. A group fitted to the largest SUBJECT BOX, which is what the review proposed, does not make the narrated sentence true: measured, beat 1's subject box is 15.685 units because its subject is {zona, trophectoderm} and the box is the ZONA's outer diameter, while beat 8's is 19.2117 with no zona at all - a ratio of 1.2249 against the narrated 1.5 and the model's 1.59. To show the ratio a student is asked to learn, the group must be fitted to a DECLARED REFERENCE MEASURE (here the embryo's own diameter, which the model already exposes as embryoD_um) rather than to whatever the beat happens to isolate. Choosing that is a schema decision with corpus scope, not a field. (b) IT SITS ON TOP OF AN ALREADY-ESCALATED FUNCTION. The distance is computed from subjectBox(), which is the subject of engine__refit-camera-on-isolate - whose reviewed round-2 fix is ABSENT from viz3d.js and which Frank has ruled must be restored by merging the hunks out of git, staying escalated until a safe lock-handling procedure exists. Four of the six beats in this comparison group (2, 3, 4, 6) isolate, so their boxes ARE the state.only boxes that item says are the wrong subject; beats 1 and 8 do not isolate. A scale group built now would be fitted across two different definitions of subject, one of them known-broken and under repair, and whoever merges those hunks would have to merge around it. See ESCALATIONS.md 2026-10-02.
items.proposed_rule: For RENDER-STANDARD section 3, beside line 124, IF AND ONLY IF the capability lands - a rule no engine can satisfy would fail every parametric process scene in the corpus on the day it is written, which is why this run did not add it: "A FIT IS PER SCENE-GROUP, NOT PER BEAT. Where beats differ in a size the narration or a claim compares, they share one camera distance, fitted to the largest value of a declared reference measure among them, and the walk reports the on-screen extent of each so an unintended normalisation shows as a flat series. A beat that must be refitted alone says so."
items.instrument_landed: viz-training/tools/measure-scene-visibility.mjs now reports box_world and world_per_px per beat and prints them on a scale: line, for every scene it walks. REPORTED, NOT GRADED, deliberately: a flat box_fill_pct beside a rising world_per_px is the signature of this defect and is now visible to any reader, but making it FAIL a beat is the standards decision above. Added by the round-5 build run on blastocyst, adopting the round-4 review's proposal ("this wants a third column, um-per-pixel, and it is one line next to the others") in world units rather than microns, so it works on a scene whose model publishes no micron scale.
items.corpus_scope: Every parametric process scene is exposed, not just this one. embryology__gametogenesis-fertilization__cleavage-morula holds the same cell-volume invariant and narrates the same journey; the folding and heart-tube scenes all narrate growth. Named by the round-4 review of blastocyst and not independently re-measured by this run - that is the next reader's first job, and the instrument to do it with is now in the tool.

items.note: MEASUREMENT-TOOL DEFECT THAT MANUFACTURES FALSE ANATOMICAL FINDINGS. Filed 2026-10-02T20:45Z by the model3d REVIEW task; the originating build run asked that it be filed as its own item. viz-training/tools/measure-scene-visibility.mjs draws the frames that reviews read, and its beauty pass sets `transparent` and `opacity` but NEVER SETS depthWrite, so three's default `true` stands - where viz3d's own adapter sets depthWrite = (opacity >= 0.98), i.e. FALSE for any authored-translucent structure. A depth-writing translucent DoubleSide sheet z-fights with what lies under it, and z-fighting breaks mirror symmetry through float rounding whose sign differs between +x and -x. CONSEQUENCE: the tool renders a structure-dependent, LEFT-RIGHT ASYMMETRIC speckle that is not in the model and that a student never sees, on models that are provably mirror-symmetric. COST ALREADY PAID: this cost trilaminar-disc-3-germ-layers two full rounds. Round 3 reported beat 6 'scratched on one side only' as a blocking-grade anatomical finding and spent its run eliminating five candidate causes; round 4 traced it to this line. MEASURED, by this review independently, mirroring each frame about its own subject centre: the TOOL's frame (player/beat06.png) gives textured fraction left 10.17% / right 21.00%, ratio 2.06; the REAL PLAYER's frame of the same beat, same t, same camera (realplayer/beat-06.png via walk-scene-in-player.mjs) gives 14.72% / 14.58%, ratio 0.99. The asymmetry is the tool's alone. FIX, one line, already proved by reversal by the originating run: add `o.material.depthWrite = s.opacity >= 0.98;` to the beauty pass. On that scene it took beat 6 from 2.86 to 1.14 and left beats 1-5, 7 and 8 PIXEL-identical, 0 changed pixels each. WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY DONE: the tool is shared, and its beauty pass feeds the alpha-aware diffKey number, so the patch can move reported visibility percentages corpus-wide; it was verified on one scene only. A run taking this should re-walk a sample of scenes and diff the reported percentages before and after. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE SCENE: this tool is the instrument reviews use to decide whether a picture is fit for a student, and it is currently capable of inventing a defect that is not in the model. Any past finding that rests on surface texture or speckle in a frame from this tool is suspect and worth re-reading.

note_neuro: The 13 neuroanatomy items were added 2026-09-10 once the old 'MedBank 3D scene author (v2)' task was confirmed to have stopped (last run 07:07 UTC, missed the two slots after it), so there is no second writer on this course. These 13 were held on MESHES that BodyParts3D does not have at the needed granularity — but they are tubes, cords and cavity casts, which is what render-kit's swept shell already does. The other 4 planned neuro scenes (cerebellum x3, brainstem x1) are foliated and nuclear, genuinely irregular, and stay a mesh problem.
policy_no_mesh_means_procedural: Frank, 2026-09-10: WHERE NO MESH EXISTS, GO PROCEDURAL IMMEDIATELY — do not leave a scene planned waiting for a mesh that is not coming. Checked against the corpus before adopting: the four cerebellum/brainstem scenes held back as 'needs a mesh' carry ZERO bodyparts3d refs between them, across 35 structures. There was nothing to wait for. The judgement that still stands is RENDER-STANDARD §5 — if the form is irregular and a student is examined on recognising it EXACTLY, say so and escalate rather than shipping a plausible fake. The rule is 'no mesh means build it', not 'no mesh means pretend'.
coverage_note: The 71 structures with NO scene were queued 2026-09-10 from tools/coverage.mjs. They are kind:'scene' — AUTHOR the VisualScene, then build whatever it needs — unlike the kind:'model3d' items above, where a scene exists and only geometry is missing. Measured basis: 207 curriculum structures declaring 397 view-slots; 136 had a scene carrying 958 views between them, 7.0 each on average, and only 2 existing scenes missed a declared view type. The corpus was never short of diagrams per topic — it was short of 71 whole structures.
policy_engine_blockers_first: 2026-10-04, escalation desk, with Frank live. THE FIVE engine__ ITEMS AT THE HEAD OF THE TODO RUN ARE THERE ON PURPOSE - DO NOT SORT THEM BACK DOWN. Measured this morning: the escalation desk held 24 items and had never released one, and the mechanical reason was that the fixes releasing them sat at the BOTTOM of this queue while 'strictly top to bottom' walked scenes. engine__procedural-ref-default-t was item 137 of 138 and embryology__week-3-gastrulation__notochord was escalated waiting for it - about 100 days out at the observed rate of roughly one item a day. Two more, engine__frame-and-light-traced-views and engine__restage-at-t, DID NOT EXIST AT ALL, so four escalated items were queued behind nothing. Landing these five releases notochord, cranio-caudal-folding, body-cavity-coelom, primitive-gut-tube and bilaminar-embryonic-disc, and repairs framing across scenes already in front of students. BEFORE STARTING ANY OF THEM: whether a build run may edit viz3d.js is NOT settled in this file. Two runs have declined on the standing 'the engine is Frank's' rule, which is why ruled engine items have sat as todo since 2026-09-29 without being taken.
